I read the complete Deepwater Horizon mishap report from the admiralty court. It was a monumental series of fuck-ups. The highlights:

  1. They tried to cement the well casing to a soft rock formation about as tough as chalk.
  2. The cement was not tested.
  3. When a gas leak from the poor cement caused a blowout, they did not act swiftly enough to stop it.
  4. Some batteries in the blowout preventer were dead.
  5. The one functioning blowout preventer had a blade too narrow to cut the drill pipe.
  6. The above-water platform had no provision for venting gas and oil outside the rig. It was designed to trap the inferno inside itself.
  7. The rig had no pressure relief panels, so the natural gas explosion caused severe structural damage.
  8. There were no cooling water sprinklers to keep the heat from weakening the steel structure.
  9. The captain had no effective mishap training and froze up. Another officer had to take charge of initial response.
  10. The rig had no watertight bulkheads to keep the flotation compartments dry. It was designed to sink in a mishap.
  11. The flotation compartments had no redundant dewatering pumps to keep them dry.

This is no what if, what if. BP had comprehensive carelessness at the time of the Deepwater Horizon mishap. They have a very high barrier of their own making to gain credibility.
